title: Kaa's Hunting
text:
In Kipling's Jungle Book, the Bandar-log, the monkey people, were noisy, boastful and leaderless. They always talked of great plans and never carried them out. One day they snatched the boy Mowgli and carried him off through the treetops to the Cold Lairs, a ruined city in the jungle.

As he was carried away, Mowgli called to Chil the kite, who flew to tell Baloo the bear and Bagheera the panther. They knew they could not handle the whole monkey horde alone, and the monkeys feared only one creature: Kaa, the great rock python. So, swallowing their pride, Baloo and Bagheera went to ask for his help, and Kaa agreed.

The three made their way to the Cold Lairs. In the moonlight, Bagheera attacked first, and the monkeys swarmed over him by the hundreds. Mowgli had been thrown into a summer house full of cobras, who left him alone after he gave the Snake People's master word. Baloo arrived and fought beside Bagheera. Then Kaa struck. He smashed through the wall of the summer house to free Mowgli, and the terrified monkeys fled to the walls.

At last Kaa began his hunger dance in the moonlight, swaying and coiling, until the monkeys, helpless and hypnotized, began to walk toward him. Baloo and Bagheera, also falling under the spell, had to be shaken awake. They led Mowgli home.
lesson: A small team that plans and brings in the right ally will beat a large, noisy crowd with no leader. Know what the opponent fears, and ask for help even when it costs you pride.
people: Mowgli, Baloo, Bagheera, Kaa, Chil the kite, the Bandar-log
location: England and the United States (story set in the jungles of central India)
source: Rudyard Kipling, The Jungle Book (1894), Kaa's Hunting
